topic: Knowledge that was never written down
hook: Every company runs on knowledge that was never written down.

shots.label: Hook
shots.say: Every company runs on knowledge that was never written down.
shots.camera: Phone vertical at eye height, arm’s length away. Look straight into the lens and stay still.
shots.onScreen: Every company runs on knowledge that was never written down.

shots.label: Problem
shots.say: Around seventy percent of company knowledge is tacit. It lives in people, not documents.
shots.camera: Keep the phone at eye height. Take one slow step toward the camera on the second sentence.

shots.label: Consequence
shots.say: Your senior engineer knows why the line fails on cold Mondays. The manual does not.
shots.camera: Move the phone to chest height for a tighter head-and-shoulders frame. Hold it steady.

shots.label: Method
shots.say: A voice-first interview captures that context in thirty to sixty minutes. A human checks it before anything is stored.
shots.camera: Sit at a desk with the phone propped vertically against a monitor, about 60 centimetres away. Gesture once toward an open notebook.

shots.label: Payoff
shots.say: The result is not perfect memory. It is a cited answer. And when it doesn’t know, it says so.
shots.camera: Return to the original eye-level position. Pause before the final sentence and hold eye contact.

caption:
The answer is already on your factory floor. It may never have reached a document.

Voice-first expert interviews capture tacit knowledge before retirement. Human review comes before storage. Answers carry citations, or none at all.

Don’t let the answer retire with the expert.
cta: Which answer in your plant still exists in only one person’s head?
soundIdea: Originalton. No music. Keep the pauses and room tone.
